handback.title: Autopilot merges by the repo's branch, method and labels
handback.summary: Autopilot merges into the repo's own branch, its own way, and reads its own labels, all from settings.
handback.user_story: Autopilot merges into my repo's branch, my way, using my label names.

acceptance_criteria.text: Autopilot merges pull requests into the default branch the settings name.

edge_cases.case: The settings name a branch GitHub does not have: nothing merges, and the reason names it.

acceptance_criteria.text: With the default branch setting left empty, autopilot merges into the repo's default branch on GitHub.

edge_cases.case: The setting is empty text rather than no value.

acceptance_criteria.text: Autopilot merges with the merge method the settings name.

edge_cases.case: GitHub holds the merge for approval: the direct merge keeps the same method.

acceptance_criteria.text: The merge gate waits for checks as many minutes as the settings say.
acceptance_criteria.no_edge_cases: A check that never finishes is the case its own test runs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Autopilot treats an issue as on autopilot by the label name in settings.

edge_cases.case: The sweep of issues on autopilot asks GitHub by that label name.
The board counts an issue on autopilot by that label name.
The owner adds the label named in settings on GitHub: the board card moves.
Filing a split from an issue on autopilot puts that label on its stories.
The up-to-date check counts an issue on autopilot by that label name.

acceptance_criteria.text: Turning autopilot on puts the label named in settings on the issue.

edge_cases.case: The board puts that label on a pull request built for an issue on autopilot.
Turning autopilot off takes the label named in settings off the issue.
Turning autopilot off on a pull request takes that label off the pull request.

acceptance_criteria.text: Dokima ships the default branch setting empty, so a repo naming none gets GitHub's default branch.
acceptance_criteria.words: ship the default branch setting empty, not "main"

edge_cases.case: A repo with no settings file at all merges into GitHub's default branch.

acceptance_criteria.text: With the default branch setting empty, workflows run on the repo's default branch on GitHub.
acceptance_criteria.words: Empty means ask GitHub for the repo's default branch

edge_cases.case: A repo that names a branch gives workflows that branch.
GitHub gives no default branch: the run stops, saying so.

answers.why: The four older fake GitHubs now name the default branch; the permission list joins the plan.
Split filing, the pull request off switch and the up-to-date check are planned and tested; the workflow is asked.
Each older fake GitHub now answers the default branch call; all fourteen pass.
The permission list joins the plan, so reading the repo maps to a read permission.
Both files join the plan, each with a new failing test.

raises.label: Workflow trigger
raises.text: A renamed autopilot label added by hand starts nothing: the autopilot workflow names autopilot. Change that workflow here? Assumed not.
raises.evidence: `.github/workflows/autopilot.yml:25` checks `github.event.label.name == 'autopilot'`; AGENTS.md forbids workflow changes unless asked.

raises.label: Doubt: already fixed
raises.text: Filed issues already carry the filed label named in settings, built by #784. Drop that ask here? Assumed yes.
